article.title: Bathroom Remodeling
article.author: Sejal Desai
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. For many homeowners, staying in a familiar home as they grow older is an important goal. A home contains memories, established routines, and connections to the surrounding community. However, a house that works well for younger adults may become more difficult to navigate as mobility, balance, strength, or vision changes over time. The bathroom is one area that deserves particular attention. Wet floors, high bathtub walls, limited lighting, and hard-to-reach fixtures can make everyday routines more challenging. Fortunately, thoughtful bathroom remodeling can improve accessibility without sacrificing comfort or style. By planning for long-term needs, homeowners can create bathrooms that are safer, easier to use, and more convenient for people of different ages and abilities. Replace a Traditional Tub With an Accessible Shower Stepping over the side of a traditional bathtub requires balance and leg strength. For older adults or anyone experiencing mobility limitations, this movement can become increasingly difficult. A walk-in or low-threshold shower can reduce the height a person needs to step over when entering the bathing area. Depending on the bathroom's construction and drainage system, homeowners may also consider a curbless shower that creates a smoother transition between the bathroom floor and shower. These designs can make bathing more convenient while giving the bathroom a clean, modern appearance. Homeowners researching Savannah GA bathroom remodeling can consider accessibility at the beginning of the planning process rather than treating it as a future modification. Incorporating easier shower access during a renovation can help create a bathroom that remains useful as household needs evolve. Add Grab Bars in Strategic Locations Grab bars are among the most practical additions to an aging-in-place bathroom. They can provide extra stability when entering or leaving the shower, standing up from the toilet, or moving through areas where floors may become wet. Placement matters, so grab bars should be installed where they provide useful support and attached securely to appropriate structural backing. Modern grab bars are available in numerous styles and finishes. Homeowners can coordinate them with faucets, shower fixtures, and other hardware, allowing safety features to become a natural part of the bathroom's overall design. Planning for grab bars during remodeling also makes it easier to provide the necessary support behind the walls. Choose Slip-Resistant Flooring Water and smooth surfaces can create a dangerous combination. Flooring should therefore be one of the first considerations when designing a bathroom for long-term use. Homeowners can choose bathroom flooring with appropriate traction, particularly around the shower, bathtub, vanity, and toilet. Shower floors should also provide stable footing when wet. The transition between different flooring materials deserves attention as well. Large changes in floor height or poorly positioned thresholds may become tripping hazards. A well-planned floor can improve safety while still supporting the desired design. Many modern flooring products are available in attractive colors, patterns, and textures, so accessibility doesn't require giving up style. Include a Built-In Shower Seat Standing for an entire shower can become tiring for some older adults. A built-in shower seat or properly designed bench can provide a comfortable place to sit while bathing. Seating can also make activities such as washing feet or legs easier and more stable. The seat should be positioned so that essential shower controls and bathing products remain within convenient reach. When combined with a handheld showerhead, a shower bench can make the bathing area significantly more flexible. Even homeowners who don't currently need seating may appreciate having it available later. Install a Handheld Showerhead A handheld showerhead is a relatively simple upgrade that can provide substantial benefits. It allows users to direct water where needed without constantly changing their body position. This is particularly useful for someone who prefers or needs to shower while seated. Handheld fixtures can also make the shower easier to clean and may be convenient for households with family members of different heights and abilities. Some shower systems combine a fixed showerhead with a handheld unit, providing flexibility without sacrificing the experience of a traditional shower. Improve Bathroom Lighting Good lighting becomes increasingly important as people age. A poorly illuminated bathroom can make it more difficult to identify wet areas, obstacles, edges, or changes in floor level. Instead of depending on one overhead fixture, homeowners can use layered lighting throughout the bathroom. Vanity lighting can improve visibility around mirrors, while dedicated shower lighting can make the bathing area easier to navigate. Low-level lighting can also help with nighttime bathroom visits. Motion-activated lighting is one option that may reduce the need to search for a switch in the dark. Natural light can be useful as well, provided privacy is maintained through appropriate windows or coverings. Make Frequently Used Items Easier to Reach Storage should be designed around accessibility rather than simply maximizing capacity. Deep cabinets may provide plenty of room, but items stored at the back can be difficult to reach. Likewise, very high shelves may require stretching or the use of a step stool. Consider drawers, pull-out organizers, accessible shelving, and recessed shower niches. Everyday products should be positioned where they can be reached comfortably without excessive bending or reaching. A more organized bathroom also reduces clutter on countertops and floors, helping keep pathways clear. Consider a Comfort-Height Toilet The height of a toilet can influence how easy it is to sit down and stand up. Some homeowners prefer comfort-height toilets because the increased seat height may make these movements easier, particularly for taller adults or people with certain mobility limitations. However, the most comfortable toilet height can vary from person to person. The fixture should be selected based on the needs of the household rather than simply choosing the tallest model available. Grab bars or other properly installed support features near the toilet can provide additional stability where appropriate. Choose Easy-to-Operate Fixtures Small details can have a major impact on bathroom usability. Traditional round faucet knobs may become difficult to grip for people experiencing reduced hand strength or dexterity. Lever-style faucets can often be operated with less twisting. Shower controls should also be positioned where they are convenient to reach. Pressure-balancing or thermostatic controls can help maintain more consistent water temperatures and reduce sudden temperature fluctuations. When selecting hardware, homeowners should consider how easily fixtures can be operated with wet hands. These details may seem minor during remodeling, but they can make daily routines considerably more comfortable. Keep the Bathroom Easy to Maintain A bathroom designed for aging in place should also be simple to clean. Numerous small grout lines, hard-to-reach corners, and complicated shower enclosures can increase maintenance requirements. Larger wall surfaces, accessible storage, and streamlined shower designs may make routine cleaning easier. Good ventilation is equally important. Bathrooms naturally produce moisture, and an appropriately sized exhaust fan can help remove humid air after showers and baths. This is particularly relevant in South Georgia, where warm and humid conditions can make moisture management an important part of bathroom planning. Plan for Accessibility Before It Becomes Necessary One advantage of remodeling early is the ability to incorporate accessible features gradually and intentionally. A homeowner may not need a shower seat, grab bars, or easier entry today, but planning for these features can reduce the need for disruptive modifications later. Accessibility improvements can also benefit visiting relatives, people recovering from injuries, and family members with temporary mobility challenges. Companies such as Five Star Bath Solutions offer bathroom remodeling services that can help homeowners explore updated bathing spaces, shower configurations, and other improvements. When discussing a renovation with any remodeling professional, homeowners can explain both their current priorities and their long-term accessibility goals so those needs can be considered during design and installation. Maintain Style While Improving Accessibility An accessible bathroom doesn't need to resemble a medical facility. Today's remodeling products allow homeowners to combine practical features with contemporary design. Grab bars can coordinate with other hardware, shower seating can complement surrounding surfaces, and low-threshold showers can create a sleek appearance. Neutral finishes can provide a timeless foundation, while mirrors, lighting, cabinet hardware, and accessories can introduce personality. The objective is to create a bathroom that feels like a comfortable part of the home while quietly incorporating features that make it easier and safer to use. Think About the Entire Bathroom Layout Individual safety features are valuable, but the overall layout matters just as much. Homeowners should consider whether there is enough open space to move comfortably between the entrance, vanity, toilet, and shower. Doors shouldn't create unnecessary obstacles, and commonly used features should be easy to reach. Where space permits, wider pathways may provide additional flexibility for someone using a cane, walker, or other mobility aid in the future. Planning the room as a complete environment rather than focusing on individual products can result in a bathroom that works more effectively over the long term. Conclusion Bathroom remodeling can play an important role in making aging in place easier. A well-designed bathroom can reduce everyday obstacles while providing greater comfort, independence, and convenience. Low-threshold showers, grab bars, slip-resistant flooring, built-in seating, handheld showerheads, improved lighting, accessible storage, and easy-to-operate fixtures are all features worth considering. Good ventilation and low-maintenance materials can further improve the bathroom's long-term usability. Most importantly, homeowners don't need to wait until accessibility becomes an urgent concern. Planning ahead provides more freedom to create a bathroom that combines safety with attractive design. By considering both current routines and future needs, homeowners can create a space that remains functional, welcoming, and comfortable through many stages of life.
